conclusion: AQL publication, fetch, dispatch admission, retirement, MQD read-index update, and completion signaling are distinct commit points and must not share one success flag.
decision: Keep B1 stopped with fetch_index=1 and dispatch_index=1 while read_index=0, retire_index=0, host_read_index_updated=false, and signal_decremented=false; make B2 prove the later commit points causally through the CU trace and output oracle.
invalidated_assumptions: Fetching and admitting a packet permits advancing the host-visible read index.
A native command-processor submission implies packet retirement or completion-signal decrement.
observation: The B1 queue accepts one publish/ring/fetch/admit sequence and rejects skipped-ring, malformed MQD, malformed packet, and in-flight unregister cases, but deliberately synthesizes no retirement and leaves the host-visible read index unchanged.
question_or_symptom: Which state transition is safe to accept before a real no-x86 CU consumer exists?
